Research Profile

Avijit Podder, PhD

Computational Scientist | Multi-Omics & Precision Medicine

University of Arizona College of Medicine - Tucson, Arizona

I develop and apply computational approaches to understand molecular heterogeneity in complex disease. My work integrates proteomic, transcriptomic, genomic, network, and clinical data to identify patient-specific molecular signatures, disease mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic hypotheses—with a particular focus on neurodegenerative disease and aging.

Research Program

From molecular complexity to individualized biology

My research spans computational biology, multi-omics integration, systems biology, and precision medicine. A central theme is moving beyond population averages to understand how molecular pathways differ across individuals and how those differences can inform disease stratification and therapeutic discovery.

01

Individualized Multi-Omics

Developing patient-centered analytical strategies that move beyond group averages to identify individual molecular signatures, pathway perturbations, and clinically meaningful heterogeneity.

02

Neurodegenerative Disease

Applying computational biology to Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, aging, and related neurological disorders with an emphasis on mechanisms, biomarkers, and disease stratification.

03

Proteomics & Transcriptomics

Integrating high-dimensional proteomic and transcriptomic data to identify molecular drivers, pathway-level changes, and candidate therapeutic targets.

04

Network & Systems Biology

Using graph theory, protein interaction networks, pathway models, and patient-similarity approaches to connect molecular variation with disease biology.

05

Cross-Species Analysis

Comparing human and model-organism molecular systems to distinguish conserved biology from species-specific effects and improve translational interpretation.

06

Computational Therapeutics

Combining omics, network analysis, molecular modeling, and data-driven prioritization to support biomarker discovery and therapeutic hypothesis generation.
